A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Perturbed Gaussian Ensemble work. Their complete text, equations, tables and figures support comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix; both end with references.

before.justification: v1 reports original CT reconstruction and novel-view-synthesis experiments, baseline comparisons and parameter ablations in Tables 1–3 and Figures 1, 3 and 4.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds lower-view-budget evaluations, additional comparison results and perturbation ablations in Tables 1–4.

M1.justification: The proposed procedure remains unchanged: perturb low-density Gaussian densities, calculate projection-space SSIM variance and select its maximizing viewpoint. Section 3 differs only editorially. Dropout and position jittering appear as experimental controls, while the proposed method and its default ensemble size remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both retain the same 15 synthetic volumes, three FIPS cases, CT reconstruction and novel-view-synthesis tasks, and hemispherical acquisition environment. v2 adds real-world novel-view scores under the unchanged per-scene test-view description, without documenting new datasets or task requirements. Smaller view budgets change experimental settings within this coverage.

E2.justification: Uniform sampling is added to the synthetic 24/36-view comparisons and the new lower-budget experiments. The original Random, FPS, TOPIQ, MANIQA, MUSIQ and FisherRF comparisons are retained. Uniform is absent from the real-world block. Table 4 additionally compares alternative perturbation controls.

E3.justification: v2 adds 6-, 8-, 12- and 16-view protocols alongside the retained 24/36-view protocols. The ensemble-size sweep changes from N={1,5,10,20} to N={5,10,15,20,40}. Existing initialization, training iterations, candidate poses, test-view count and evaluation metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v1 studies the uncertainty metric and N/alpha/beta sensitivity. v2 substantially extends component validation through Table 4, comparing density scaling with dropout, position jittering and their combination at two view budgets. It also extends ensemble-size sensitivity and tests performance at substantially smaller acquisition budgets in Table 2.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental replicate counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The revised ensemble-size sweep concerns an algorithmic parameter; it does not document additional independent experimental runs or a changed statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: All original numerical entries from v1 Tables 1–2 are retained in v2 Table 1. Substantial new results cover Uniform, real-world novel-view synthesis, lower view budgets and perturbation alternatives; Table 3 removes N=1 and adds N=15/40. Uniform becomes the strongest synthetic 3D PSNR baseline, reducing the reported method's lead to 0.516/0.349 dB at 24/36 views, although Section 4.2 retains the old 'up to 0.68 dB' statement.

T1.justification: Equations 1–15, including the radiative model, posterior approximation, perturbation distribution and variance-based acquisition rule, are unchanged. No mathematical definitions, assumptions, proofs or derivations are substantively added or revised.

C1.justification: The introduction adds an explicit claim that the framework is designed for flexible C-arm CT systems, refining its intended application. The abstract, contribution list and conclusion otherwise retain the same methodological and performance claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 now identifies N=10 or 15 as the preferred trade-off and discusses degradation at N=40, whereas v1 singled out N=10 and discussed N=20. A new paragraph attributes dropout and position-jittering results to misleading uncertainty estimates. The existing mechanism explanations otherwise remain.

D1.justification: The promised GitHub code-release link in v1 is replaced by a project-page link in v2; the PDFs do not establish actual code availability. Section 4.1 corrects alpha=10 to alpha=10%, consistent with v1's method description and ablation table. Optimizer, hardware and other implementation disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 acknowledges prior CT uncertainty estimation and active acquisition through references 67 and 88, including ActiveNAF, refining the gap to radiative Gaussian Splatting. It also adds ensemble, self-ensembling and online-learning references and an explicit continual/online-learning connection, while removing HDR-GS. The overall positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: The section sequence and most prose are retained. Changes include brief related-work and experimental additions, grammar corrections, a shorter running header, rearranged author-contact information and expanded acknowledgements. There is no extensive narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: The experimental displays are substantially reorganized: v1 Tables 1–2 merge into an expanded v2 Table 1, new Tables 2 and 4 are introduced, and Table 3 changes from a narrow side float to a full-width, two-block layout. Table captions move above the displays. Figures 1–4 remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added Uniform baseline, lower-budget evaluations and perturbation controls strengthen the empirical justification for the acquisition strategy, while acknowledging prior CT work improves positioning. These gains are limited by missing uncertainty estimates and sparse implementation detail for the new perturbation controls. v2 also introduces a reporting inconsistency by retaining the 0.68 dB second-best margin after Uniform narrows that advantage. The net improvement is useful but limited.
